_meta.purpose: Durable hand-researched overlay merged into draft-board.json by build-draft-board.mjs. Survives ADP rebuilds. Web-sourced 2026-07-20; re-verify injury/flag status in the final 2 weeks before draft.
_meta.risk_flags_semantics: true = documented exposure; false = researched, no current exposure; researched:true means it was checked. Clean designation = not surfaced in the league-wide suspension/holdout sweep AND clean games-played — a reasonable confidence level, not a per-player deep dive.
_meta.injury_history_null: rookies / <1 NFL season — no history exists; page shows 'no data' rather than a guess
_meta.scouting_seed: Top-tier scouting_brief seed (13 players by ADP), web-sourced 2026-07-21. Scheme-fit-first prose + role_stability/scheme_fit/override_flag. Retrieval-grounded; extend deeper as the draft nears. null below = not scouted yet.

2133.injury_history: Missed time 2024-25 (14/14); age 33 — decline + durability is the compound risk.
2133.adp_commentary: WR at ~55. Name value; an age-33 WR is a steep redraft bet and the board rates him below ADP — a fade in this ceiling-over-name format.

2216.injury_history: Age-33 season coming off injuries and his worst fantasy year (10.6 PPG, WR41); 1.62 YPRR is a separate red flag. Durability plus age-decline is the compound risk.
2216.adp_commentary: WR at ~57 — name value on an age-33 receiver coming off his worst season and now in a new SF role; the board likely rates him below ADP. A fade in this ceiling-over-name format.

3198.injury_history: Remarkably durable (17/17/17); the flag is age (32), not health.
3198.adp_commentary: RB at ~22 — an age-32 RB is the archetypal cliff bet, but his workload and BAL offense have shown no decline; the board rates him a clear RB1 and the durability is a genuine plus.

scouting_brief.prose: Still Baltimore's workhorse and still elite by Next Gen Stats after a 1,595-yard, 16-TD, 307-carry 2025, with Lamar Jackson keeping defenses honest. The case against is age and mileage: he enters his age-32 season with 2,800+ career touches, where aging curves say decline is overdue, and a new coaching staff plus a remade interior offensive line add uncertainty. He's defied the curve so far and stayed durable (17 games three years running); analysts still peg him a mid-to-late first-round RB1.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked workhorse, still elite by NGS; age-32 + 2,800 career touches + a new staff/remade interior O-line are the caps, but he's defied the aging curve and stayed durable.

3294.injury_history: 2024 catastrophic hamstring (torn off the bone, Week 8, season-ending surgery — 8 games). Returned fully in 2025 (17 games, Comeback Player of the Year finalist).
3294.adp_commentary: QB at ~97.8 — the 2024 injury is fully behind him (a healthy 17-game 2025 proves it); with the offense intact he's a solid streaming-plus QB, though the 1-QB caveat applies.

4034.injury_history: 2024 lost 13 games to bilateral Achilles tendinitis (soft-tissue, both legs) + late PCL sprain; answered with a 17-game RB1 season in 2025. Age 30 + Achilles history is the recurrence/decline risk, not a current injury.
4034.adp_commentary: Market drafts him ~RB5 (ADP 5.7) while the board values him ~RB9 — you're paying up for ceiling against an age-30, Achilles-history availability cap. A slight reach at cost in a format where RB-adjacent value is available later.

scouting_brief.prose: When healthy he's a full-usage centerpiece in Shanahan's offense — 2025's No. 1 non-QB at 24.5 PPG on ~450 total touches. The scouting story is risk, not role: an age-30 season, extensive injury history, and a workload history says regresses (~48% avg decline after 370+ touches). SF plans to be 'cautious' through camp; analysts near-unanimously recommend handcuffing his backup.
scouting_brief.rationale: Role/scheme elite; the flag is age-30 + workload + injury history (uncertainty, not role).

4037.injury_history: 2024 season-ending dislocated/fractured ankle that also delayed and wrecked 2025 (9 PPG over injury-hit games). ~30 games missed across 9 seasons. Reportedly enters 2026 healthy.
4037.adp_commentary: WR at ~93 — was a 19.7-PPG player before the ankle; if fully healthy that's a massive value at WR36 ADP, but the ankle wrecked a year-plus and the durability history is long. A high-variance value pick.

4046.injury_history: 2025 torn ACL + LCL (Week 15). Throwing this offseason and targeting Week 1, but KC has stopped short of guaranteeing that date — real Week-1 risk on a structural knee.
4046.adp_commentary: QB at ~101 — name-brand QB coming off a torn ACL+LCL with an uncertain Week 1; in a 1-QB streaming league there is no reason to pay QB1-name prices for that risk. Let someone else.

4199.injury_history: 2025 limited to 12 games (combination of injuries incl. a Week 18 hip); age 31. Age + accumulating soft-tissue is the profile.

notes: Restructured to stay in MIN for 2026.

4199.adp_commentary: RB at ~107 — an aging back in a timeshare with Jordan Mason; little upside unless injury clears the way. Depth/bye filler at cost.

4217.injury_history: MAJOR: ruptured his Achilles on Jan 11 2026. Likely opens on Reserve/PUP and misses ~the first month; turns 33 in October. A fringe-TE1 finish would be 'borderline miraculous' per analysts.
4217.adp_commentary: TE at ~99 — do not draft as a starter. A ruptured Achilles at 33 with real PUP/first-month risk makes him a late-round stash for the playoff run at best, not the every-week TE1 his name implies. You (ThatWasButtery) rostered him in 2025 — this is a clear sell/avoid at cost.

4866.injury_history: Durable recently (14/16/16), no chronic pattern; the flag is age (29) not health.
4866.adp_commentary: RB at ~15.4. Age-29 RBs are the classic cliff risk, but the PHI O-line + recent workload keep him a fringe RB1 — fair, not a bargain.

scouting_brief.prose: Bell-cow role locked (79% snap share, 70% of the rush attempts in 2025), and new OC Sean Mannion is expected to put Hurts under center more often — a wrinkle Barkley says he's eager for and one the numbers suggest boosts his efficiency. The 2025 dip tracked an offensive line that fell from 9th to 16th in run-block win rate; a healthy line plus the scheme tweak point to a bounce-back. Age 29 and the 2024 workload are the only real caps; consensus has him mid-first to early-second.
scouting_brief.rationale: Bell-cow role locked; Mannion's under-center scheme + a healthy O-line point to a bounce-back, age-29 the only cap.

4881.adp_commentary: QB at ~39.6 — the format's premium QB archetype (rushing floor immune to the 4-pt passing-TD cap). Same 1-QB caveat: the streamer band is free, so pay only for the ceiling.

4984.adp_commentary: QB1 at ~24.2 — but in a 1-QB, 10-team league QB13-16 stream free all year. The board's VORP likes the player, not the pick: only worth it if you value his konami-rushing floor over the RB/WR you'd pass at that slot.

5850.injury_history: 2025 knee (missed Weeks 11-12; noticeably less effective after — 14.6 touches/11.3 pts vs 21.1/19.6 before).

notes: Arrested May 27 2026, five charges incl. felony strangulation (alleged domestic, Brown County WI); released same day. DA has NOT decided on charges — investigation ongoing.
Commissioner-Exempt-list / suspension exposure while unresolved; if charges are declined he'll likely avoid suspension, but this is a live, unresolved legal + availability risk.

5850.adp_commentary: RB at ~25.2 — top-12 RB talent, but a pending domestic-violence case (felony charge, undecided) plus a 2025 knee that sapped his second half make this a genuine avoid-until-clarity at cost. The ADP has not fully absorbed the legal risk.

5859.injury_history: Missed some time 2024-25 (13/15) — minor hamstring/knee, not chronic.
5859.adp_commentary: WR at ~24.4. Now in New England with Drake Maye (traded from PHI); target dominance intact but the offense downgrade caps the ceiling — a mild reach at ADP 16-range boards, fairer here at 24.

scouting_brief.prose: Now the clear No. 1 for Drake Maye after the trade to New England, and the move reads as a scheme upgrade rather than the downgrade some feared: the Patriots ranked 9th in neutral pass rate (Philly 15th) and 15th in pass rate inside the 10 (Philly 32nd), so his touchdown fuel actually rises, and Maye led the NFL in completion rate and yards per attempt in 2025. Brown has finished top-7 in target share seven straight years; analysts see top-five upside. Role locked, scheme a plus.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked WR1 for Maye; NE is a pass-rate/red-zone upgrade over PHI — more bullish than the standing adp_commentary's 'downgrade' read.

notes: Live training-camp holdout for a new deal (unresolved as of this research). Fined per day; missed-camp/games risk until settled.

5927.adp_commentary: WR at ~58.8. A live holdout depresses the ADP: upside is a solid WR2 if the deal gets done and he reports on time, downside is missed camp and early games. Do not draft until the holdout resolves.

6770.injury_history: 2025 limited to 8 games (turf-toe surgery). When healthy a top-5 fantasy QB — but that version has shown up once in three seasons; the injury history is the story.
6770.adp_commentary: QB at ~58 — elite ceiling with Chase + Higgins, but in this 1-QB streaming league you pay only for the healthy-Burrow ceiling, and the availability track record makes that a real gamble.

6786.injury_history: High-ankle/shoulder issues cost games in 2025 (14); not a chronic pattern.
6786.adp_commentary: WR at ~10.3. Target hog; Pickens opposite him (now on the franchise tag, participating) is only mild competition.

scouting_brief.prose: Still the most talented WR in a pass-heavy Dallas offense (2nd in NFL passing) with Dak Prescott healthy and full scheme continuity under Schottenheimer — the setup to reclaim his 17+ PPG form after an injury-and-Pickens-hit 2025. The cap is real target competition: George Pickens drew 137 targets last year, so both can eat but Lamb's ceiling isn't the uncontested 2023 version. Locked-in Round-1 WR1.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked WR1 with Dak + continuity; Pickens target competition caps the ceiling.

6794.injury_history: 2023 hamstring (IR, soft-tissue — reinjury-prone class); durable since (17/17). Annual hamstring-flare watch.
6794.adp_commentary: WR at ~12.4. Top-3 talent; the MIN QB question (Murray/McCarthy) and the hamstring history are the only caps on an otherwise top-5 profile.

scouting_brief.prose: Uncontested target hog even in a dysfunctional 2025, so the read is the new quarterback: Minnesota added Kyler Murray to compete with — and likely beat out — second-year J.J. McCarthy, and Jefferson has stayed neutral while building chemistry with both. Analysts frame the Murray arrival as a rebound path back to the elite WR1 tier, but at least one insider tags him a risky early pick given Murray's 6.0 yards per attempt and low TD rate in 2025 plus a rushing profile that can suppress raw target volume. Talent and target share are locked; the QB resolution is the swing on his ceiling.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked target share; the Murray/McCarthy QB question is the ceiling swing, and it's broadly priced.

6797.injury_history: Durable-ish (13/17/16); no chronic pattern. New Mike McDaniel run-first scheme (quicker release, ~2.4s time-to-throw) trims pass volume.
6797.adp_commentary: QB at ~85.7 — the scheme change compresses his passing volume in a format that already caps pocket QBs (4-pt TD, 1/25 yds); a streamer-band QB here unless his mobility becomes a designed-run element.

6801.injury_history: Recurring soft-tissue history — hamstring (missed 2 to start a season) and a high-ankle sprain (3 games); expected 100% for Week 1. Perennial 'needs better injury luck' profile.
6801.adp_commentary: WR at ~37.8 — elite TD source (career-high 11 TDs even with Burrow hurt in 2025); the recurring soft-tissue history is the cap on an otherwise back-end-WR1 ceiling.

6806.injury_history: Chronically injury-prone — long Achilles history plus a Nov 2025 foot injury that required a second opinion. gp 1/13/10 over three years. Now in a crowded Denver backfield.
6806.adp_commentary: RB at ~90.6 — talent flashes, but the availability record is among the worst on the board and the backfield is crowded (Harvey, rookie Coleman). A late-round dart, not a plan.

6813.injury_history: Recurring high-ankle sprains (2022 surgery, 2024 re-injury) — a documented re-injury pattern; played 17 in 2025, currently healthy.
6813.adp_commentary: RB at ~6.4. Led the NFL in carries in 2025 — bell-cow volume is elite here — with the high-ankle recurrence history as the cap rather than a live concern.

scouting_brief.prose: Still the focal point of the Colts' run game (league-high 323 carries, all 17 games in 2025), with Daniel Jones back from an Achilles tear to stabilize the offense. The live watch is a public staff split: RB coach DeAndre Smith says they 'need to find ways to take some of that workload off,' while HC Steichen resists — unresolved. If a committee forms it dents the projection; for now he's the overwhelming touch leader.
scouting_brief.rationale: Workhorse role intact but a public workload-reduction push is unresolved — monitor.

7523.injury_history: 2024 shoulder issues (10 games); healthy 17 in 2025 under Liam Coen. No lingering concern reported.
7523.adp_commentary: QB at ~93.8 — top-10 QB upside in Year 2 of the Coen offense; the 2024 shoulder is behind him. Standard 1-QB-league caveat: streamer band is free, so pay only for the ceiling.

7526.injury_history: Frequent nagging (soft-tissue) injuries throughout his Miami tenure; no single structural event, but a chronic availability drag. Now in Denver.
7526.adp_commentary: WR at ~45.5 — a featured role in an ascending Denver pass game is the breakout case; the chronic nagging-injury pattern is the reason he keeps hovering on the WR1 fringe rather than breaking through.

7547.adp_commentary: WR at ~8.6. Volume + TD equity in a high-scoring Detroit offense; only mild target competition caps him.

scouting_brief.prose: Detroit's locked-in target hog — four straight 1,100-yard seasons and 10+ TDs in three straight — with Jared Goff still throwing. The watch is scheme continuity: John Morton was dismissed and Drew Petzing is his new (and fifth career) play-caller; St. Brown himself cautioned the offense 'won't click right away.' Talent and volume float the floor, but early-season timing is a mild question.
scouting_brief.rationale: Elite role secure; new OC Petzing + 'won't click right away' is the only drag.

7564.adp_commentary: WR1 at ~3.7. Elite target share; in half-PPR his yardage/TD profile survives the reception haircut — correctly priced top-4 overall.

scouting_brief.prose: Scheme-proof WR1 in one of the NFL's premier passing offenses: 30%+ target share and an NFL-high 185 targets even through 2025's QB instability. Burrow projects back to full strength and Tee Higgins re-signed (4yr/$115M), keeping the offense's shape intact — analysts call him one of the safest, highest ceilings at the position. Only watch is Burrow's health (turf toe cost most of 2025).
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked target hog; offense intact with Burrow healthy + Higgins retained.

7569.injury_history: MISSED TIME IN ALL FIVE NFL SEASONS — chronic soft-tissue availability concern. Ceiling is a Tier-1 WR if he ever plays 17.
7569.adp_commentary: WR at ~23.7. The talent says top-10 WR; the availability record says round 3. The highest injury-bust risk in the WR2 tier — a boom-or-miss-weeks pick this format's ceiling-hunting rewards, but eyes open.

scouting_brief.prose: Houston's unquestioned WR1 — a third 1,000-yard season in four years and a top-10 fantasy finish in 2025, projected for 128 targets. The scheme read is neutral: OC Nick Caley's attack got a bit more conservative but pass attempts still rose, and a C.J. Stroud bounce-back is the clear ceiling-raiser (Collins actually produced without him). A potential Tank Dell return plus Higgins/Noel could make this his most crowded target room, a mild cap. Availability is his separate, well-documented risk.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked WR1; a Stroud bounce-back is the upside, a more conservative scheme + a potentially crowded room the caps (availability tracked separately).

8112.injury_history: Missed games in 2025 (12); a 'Questionable' tag is carrying in Sleeper's DB — verify at camp.
8112.adp_commentary: WR at ~17.6. Ascending target share in ATL; the Penix/Tua QB battle is the swing factor on his ceiling.

scouting_brief.prose: Locked-in WR1 and target hog — the WR6 in points per game through Week 10 last year before a PCL injury ended his season — with top-five upside if the quarterback shakes out. That's the whole question: Michael Penix Jr. has seemingly taken the lead after a Tua Tagovailoa injury but is dealing with his own camp injury, so the offense's QB is unsettled entering the season. London and Kyle Pitts both produced through shaky QB play in 2025, which is the case his talent carries the role regardless.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked WR1 target hog; the Penix/Tua QB uncertainty is the ceiling swing, and he produced through bad QB play in 2025.

8130.adp_commentary: TE at ~20.3. Elite target share; in a 1-TE league an every-week TE1 is worth round-2 capital given the replacement cliff — but the ARI QB uncertainty is a caveat, and rival Stipe now chases early TEs.

scouting_brief.prose: Coming off a record tight-end season (126 catches, 1,239 yards, 11 TDs) and still the locked-in centerpiece of the Arizona passing game. The QB downgrade is real — Kyler Murray is gone, with Jacoby Brissett the likely starter ahead of Minshew and Beck — and new HC Mike LaFleur's scheme should be more run-balanced. But McBride already broke out catching passes from two different QBs, and LaFleur's 12-personnel (two-tight-end) sets keep his target volume elevated even in a more balanced attack.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked elite TE target hog; QB downgrade (Murray out, Brissett in) + a more balanced scheme are offset by heavy 12-personnel usage.

notes: On the fully-guaranteed $27.3M franchise tag; attended minicamp, no holdout — resolved.

8137.adp_commentary: WR at ~27.1. Contract-year motivation as the WR2 opposite CeeDee in Dallas; his TD-lean profile plays up in half-PPR.

8138.adp_commentary: RB at ~8.2. Went RB6→RB-adjacent on Brady's continuity in Buffalo; TD-dependent but the board rates him a clear value vs ADP.

scouting_brief.prose: Contract secure (4yr/$48M) as Buffalo's lead back, with Joe Brady — now HC — running the run-friendly, free-flowing style that fueled Cook's TD spike. But regression signals stack up: 16 rush TDs is unsustainable, lead blocker Reggie Gilliam left, the O-line has left-guard/tackle turnover, and DJ Moore was traded in for more target competition. Role is safe; the efficiency/TD profile is the risk the projection may carry too high.
scouting_brief.rationale: Lead-back role locked; TD regression + lost blocker + new mouths cap the upside.

8144.injury_history: MAJOR RED FLAG: 4-5 diagnosed concussions (2022-2024; missed 9 games in 2024) PLUS a January-2026 blood clot in the lung, limited in offseason work. Concussion recurrence + clot is the board's most serious availability profile.

notes: Contract year in NO; hold-in chatter given health, but speculative.

8144.adp_commentary: WR at ~31.8. Pure talent is a top-15 WR, but a 4-5 concussion history plus an offseason pulmonary blood clot make this arguably the riskiest availability profile on the board — the ADP does NOT fully price the medical risk. Let someone else chase the upside.

8146.injury_history: 2025 hyperextended knee (November), shut down/IR — only 7 games. One-off structural, targeting full health for 2026; not a chronic pattern.
8146.adp_commentary: WR at ~40.5. Bounce-back candidate — the knee cost 2025 but isn't chronic; the NYJ QB situation is the real cap on his rebound.

notes: Repeat offender: 4-game gambling suspension (2023) + 2-game PED suspension (2024). A PED repeat escalates to a 17-game ban — genuine week-loss exposure. No confirmed 2026 suspension, but documented exposure per the user's 'suspension exposure' flag.

8148.adp_commentary: WR at ~52.2. Legitimate big-play, per-game upside — but the two-suspension history (especially PED, where a second strike is a full-season ban) is real exposure the ADP treats lightly. Flagged, not disqualified.

8151.injury_history: Lower-body/abdomen injuries missed time 2022-24; first fully clean 17-game season in 2025. Signed with KC (new scheme) in 2026.
8151.adp_commentary: RB at ~16.8. Three straight partial seasons before 2025 plus a KC scheme change cap him; the ADP fairly bakes in the durability question.

scouting_brief.prose: Fresh three-year deal to be Kansas City's bell-cow, and Andy Reid — historically a lean-on-one-back coach (Charles, McCoy, early Hunt) — appears set to hand him 15-18 carries plus goal-line work with Hunt and Pacheco gone. Clear runway in a strong RB scheme; Mahomes's presence (back from a torn ACL) keeps defenses honest. Watches: the Mahomes health question, a brand-new system, and Walker's spotty durability; one analyst calls the early 2nd-round ADP a touch rich.
scouting_brief.rationale: Bell-cow role in a back-friendly Reid scheme; Mahomes health + new system the caveats.

8167.injury_history: 20 games missed over 4 seasons — but the recurring hamstrings were tied to a biomechanical asymmetry reportedly corrected ~2 years ago, and his ACL was a 'clean' tear. Enters 2026 fully healthy for the first time in a while.
8167.adp_commentary: WR at ~63 — a real breakout dart if the corrected biomechanics hold; the injury history says buyer-beware, but the cause (not just the symptom) was addressed, which is more encouraging than the raw games-missed suggests.

8183.injury_history: 2025 missed time (9 games); cause not separately verified this pass. SF left-guard turnover (protection) is a separate 2026 risk.
8183.adp_commentary: QB at ~105.8 — a pocket QB in a strong scheme, but the 2025 availability and O-line questions cap him; standard 1-QB streamer here.

9221.injury_history: Minor 2023 (15 games), 17/17 since — no chronic pattern.
9221.adp_commentary: RB2 at ~2.9. Campbell's 'bell cow now' comments consolidate his touches — the single most valuable RB signal in this format — so a top-3 price is correct.

scouting_brief.prose: HC Dan Campbell has publicly named him 'our bell cow now,' and David Montgomery's departure clears the backfield — genuine touch consolidation, the top value signal in this format. Consensus RB1-overall candidate. Watch: Detroit signed Isiah Pacheco, who could absorb some early-down/goal-line work, and there's OC turnover (Morton out, Petzing in) as a mild scheme unknown.
scouting_brief.rationale: Bell-cow per HC + Montgomery gone; Pacheco a minor goal-line hedge.

9224.injury_history: 2023 rookie limited (12 games); 16/17 since — trending durable.
9224.adp_commentary: RB at ~19.1 — one of the board's biggest RB values vs ADP. CIN volume + a clean recent workload make him a target a full round after his value rank.

scouting_brief.prose: Locked into the top of the Cincinnati backfield in a contract year, behind an offensive line that returns all five starters. Joe Burrow endorsed him at camp as 'a close second' to Ja'Marr Chase in getting the ball, signaling continued heavy usage, with only Samaje Perine and 2025 sixth-rounder Tahj Brooks behind him. Coming off back-to-back double-digit-TD seasons; a healthy Burrow keeps the floor high and a run-leaning philosophical shift could lift the ceiling.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked lead back; Burrow calling him 'a close second' for the ball + a returning O-line and a run-leaning shift point up.

9226.injury_history: 2023 rookie knee (11 games); 17 then 16 since. A 'Questionable' tag is carrying in Sleeper's DB — verify at camp, likely stale.
9226.adp_commentary: RB at ~13.6. Receiving-back volume plays slightly down in half-PPR vs full-PPR ADP, but Miami's lead role keeps him a low-end RB1.

scouting_brief.prose: Role is secure — he's the clear lead back (neither Jaylen Wright nor rookie Ollie Gordon threatened him), and OC Slowik may lean on him even harder. But the scheme signals are negative: Mike McDaniel, who built his pass-game role, is gone, and QB Malik Willis is a runner whose scrambles replace RB checkdowns and whose goal-line rushing eats Achane's TDs — analysts already tag him a 2026 'faller.' A real receiving/TD downgrade the projection may not fully reflect.
scouting_brief.rationale: QB/scheme downgrade (Tua→Willis, McDaniel gone) likely trims his receiving + goal-line role below the projection — revisit.

9484.injury_history: 2025 missed time (8 games); cause not separately verified this pass — flagged for re-check.
9484.adp_commentary: TE at ~68 — an ascending GB TE; the 2025 games-missed is the availability question. A mid-round TE dart with real upside if healthy.

9488.adp_commentary: WR2 at ~7.3. Led the NFL with ~44% of Seattle's air yards in 2025 — format-correct here (yardage-driven, survives half-PPR). The pick your team name already endorses.

scouting_brief.prose: Unquestioned Seattle WR1 off a historic 2025 (WR2, NFL-high 36% target share, 1,793 yds), with Sam Darnold back and no new pass-catchers added to threaten his usage. The one wrinkle is scheme: OC Klint Kubiak left for Las Vegas, replaced by Brian Fleury (ex-49ers TE coach) — analysts don't expect it to tank him but flag the play-caller change. Floor is high given his first-read target dominance.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked WR1, no new target competition; the OC change (Kubiak out) is the only unknown.

9493.injury_history: 2024 PCL sprain (knee), re-aggravated from a joint practice, missed 6+; played 16 in 2025. Re-aggravation pattern is the watch.
9493.adp_commentary: WR at ~4.8. Elite when healthy; the PCL re-aggravation history plus Rams target competition cap an otherwise top-3 WR profile.

scouting_brief.prose: Stafford's clear #1 (Kupp gone) in McVay's elite offense, coming off a league-leading 23.4 PPG. Scheme fit isn't a clean plus, though: Davante Adams is a goal-line savant (14 TDs in 2025) who caps Nacua's TD ceiling, and one analyst framed the new-look offense as a mild drag on his outlook. Off-field note: an offseason rehab stint, but no on-field concern reported.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked target leader; Adams's goal-line role is the TD-ceiling cap.

notes: Extension-leverage chatter (agent pushing for highest-paid RB) but participating; no holdout.

9509.adp_commentary: RB1 off the board at ~1.5. In a 2-RB/2-FLEX half-PPR league the elite bell-cow RB is the scarcest resource (top VORP tier), and Bijan's clean availability + workhorse role justify 1.01 cost despite Atlanta's stated wide-zone usage-cap talk.

scouting_brief.prose: Stefanski's wide-zone/gap scheme and 12-personnel sets suit him, and Tyler Allgeier's departure opens goal-line carries — analysts see a possible TD bump, with CBS calling the outlook 'complicated' only re: a lighter touch-share, not his standing. Consensus locked-in RB1 who can win a week by himself. Lone watch: Stefanski trimming his 35%+ usage share, but the projection already assumes elite volume.
scouting_brief.rationale: Centerpiece role secure; scheme + Allgeier's exit are mild positives already largely priced.

9756.injury_history: Durable on the field (17/15/14); the 2025 dip was a suspension, not injury.

notes: Served a 3-game suspension to open 2025 (Substances-of-Abuse policy, from a 2024 DUI resolved as a 'wet reckless' misdemeanor). Eligible with no remaining 2026 ban — but a second policy violation would escalate. Documented, currently resolved (like Rice).

9756.adp_commentary: WR at ~98.4 — the WR2 in a strong MIN passing game; the suspension is served and behind him. A steady value at cost, with the substance-policy history as a background note, not a live flag.

10222.injury_history: 2025 missed time (7 games); cause not separately verified this pass — flagged for re-check.
10222.adp_commentary: WR at ~110.5 — big-play GB slot; the 2025 availability plus a crowded target tree cap him. Late-round upside dart.

10229.injury_history: 2024 knee (LCL, 4 games) then a 2026 offseason knee clean-up (~2 months, debris removal). Verify the knee clears camp.

notes: Served a 6-game conduct suspension in 2025 (2024 Dallas crash); NOT expected to be suspended again.
Completed a 30-day jail term (May 2026, probation violation) and was released; legal matter resolved.

10229.adp_commentary: WR at ~34.8 (~WR12). The ADP has already absorbed the jail stint and the knee — he's elite on the field, and the price IS the discount. A calculated-risk value if the knee clears camp; the conduct/legal history is documented but currently resolved.

10236.injury_history: Missed time in 2024-25 (13/12 games) — nagging soft-tissue/lower-body issues, no single structural event.
10236.adp_commentary: TE at ~97.5 — talent for a top-8 TE, but the availability and a crowded BUF target tree cap him; fine as a mid-round TE swing.

scouting_brief.prose: Back to full health after a 2025 knee injury capped him at 84-630-7, and set up as the clear No. 1 pass-game option in Las Vegas. New HC Klint Kubiak — fresh off coordinating the Super Bowl champion Seahawks — has a strong tight-end track record (Kittle in San Francisco) and publicly made getting the most out of Bowers a priority; analysts project 130+ targets and a real path back to TE1-overall. Healthy role and scheme both point up.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked No. 1 target, healthy again; Kubiak's TE-friendly scheme (Kittle pedigree) points to a TE1-overall ceiling.

11632.adp_commentary: WR at ~24.6. Elite talent at a discount IF healthy — but the ACL recovery is the entire bet. This format overpays for uninjured elite WRs, and he isn't one yet; draft the discount only if you can carry the IR stash.

scouting_brief.prose: Emerged as the Chargers' lead back as a 2025 rookie once Najee Harris went down (4.4 YPC with steady pass-game work), and profiles as the early-down runner in Greg Roman's run-heavy scheme. The cap is a real committee: Roman favors an RB rotation, the room is deep (Kimani Vidal retained plus added competition), and a 2025 ankle limited Hampton to nine games. Talent supports a lead role, but the touch ceiling is held down by the rotation and his own durability question.
scouting_brief.rationale: Likely lead back in a run-heavy scheme, but Roman's rotation approach + a deep room + a 2025 ankle cap the bell-cow ceiling.

12527.adp_commentary: RB at ~11.9 — projected rookie workhorse in LV. No availability history to lean on, so the projection carries all the weight; rookie variance applies.

scouting_brief.prose: Clear scheme upgrade: Chip Kelly is out as OC, and Klint Kubiak's system (81+ backfield receptions/yr since 2021) plus a rebuilt line (added C Tyler Linderbaum) point to three-down workhorse usage. RB coach says he's 'doing all the right things' for a full workhorse role; 4th-round rookie Mike Washington is only a pusher. Consensus bounce-back from a disappointing RB16 rookie year to top-10 upside.
scouting_brief.rationale: Workhorse + Kubiak pass-game usage + better scheme/OL; only a late-round pusher behind him.

clean_researched.note: Swept in the league-wide suspension/holdout pass (nothing found) AND games-played durable. The build script sets researched-clean flags and derives injury_history from games-played (rookies -> null, since no NFL history exists). This is a reasonable confidence level, NOT a per-player medical deep dive.
